card.name: Letter T starting a new word part
card.fires_on: A capital or lowercase T (often after a hyphen or space) that begins a new word, where the next letters are likely 'tre', 'tu', 'ta' and so on. It appears in hyphenated or abbreviated terms like anti-TB, post-treatment, Stoke-on-Trent, T. brucei.

modes.label: Hyphen then T
modes.description: A hyphen followed by T or t that starts the second part of a compound.
modes.example: Alternative treatment for clarithromycin should be considered when treating patients receiving rifabutin ANTI<<-T>>B (Tuberculosis) Ethamb

modes.label: Abbreviated genus T.
modes.description: A lone T standing for a genus name such as Trypanosoma or Treponema.
modes.example: due to<< T>>. brucei gambiense disease

modes.label: Stray t at word start
modes.description: A lowercase or capital t that opens a word in ordinary text.
modes.example: allowing them to take a huge swipe at the<< t>>ills themselves.

card.writes: It pushes the next piece toward words beginning with 'tre', such as treasury or treasure.
card.plain: It marks a T that begins a new word part, often after a hyphen, like anti-TB or post-treatment.
